office_does: The Clark County Council adopts the county budget and property-tax levies, sets councilmanic taxes and fees, adopts the growth-management comprehensive plan and land-use rules for unincorporated areas, and decides which county propositions go to voters.
race_blurb: Open seat left by Council Chair Sue Marshall. Battle Ground councilor and former mayor Troy McCoy faces Charter Review Commissioner Peter Silliman; both stress public safety and caution on taxes, but split on a charter amendment requiring a council supermajority for taxes and on growth regulation.

candidates.summary: Battle Ground city councilor, former mayor and former school board president, and a small-business owner, who stresses managed growth, jail capacity and collaboration.
highlights: "I don't think there's a lot of room for tax increases"; opposes the tax-supermajority charter amendment as too high a bar [S9]
As mayor, voted with the unanimous Battle Ground council for a 0.1% public-safety sales tax to add police officers [S8]
Calls current jail capacity unacceptable and wants outside funding pursued before taxpayers [S3]
Opposes industrial development on farmland and in rural Brush Prairie [S3]
Endorsed by The Columbian and Council Chair Sue Marshall [S11][S6]

taxes.basis: Cautions against tax increases and wants outside funding first, but voted as mayor for a councilmanic police sales tax and opposes a tax supermajority.

safety.basis: Emphasizes police staffing, equipment and jail capacity within what he calls a holistic approach.

experience.basis: School board, city council and mayoral record; runs on "proven and effective leadership."

candidates.summary: Elected Charter Review Commissioner, former county council policy analyst and communications consultant, and a Republican precinct committee officer, running on tax restraint, budget accountability and law enforcement.
highlights: Criticizes the council's maximum levy increases and sales tax; supports requiring four of five councilors to raise taxes [S5][S17]
Chairs the committees for Charter Amendments 20 (budget transparency) and 27 (performance audits), which he sponsored; opposes Charter Amendment 22 [S11][S12][S13]
Would revisit county GMA restrictions beyond state law and limit permitting timelines [S3]
Co-sponsored a charter amendment to require deputy staffing; "citizens must elect unapologetically pro law enforcement representatives" [S9][S6]

taxes.basis: "Protection from tax increases" platform, criticism of maximum levy and sales-tax increases, and support for a council tax supermajority.

spending.basis: Authored the performance-audit and budget-transparency amendments and pledges to find non-essential services to cut.

housing.basis: Attributes high home costs to GMA, impact fees, zoning, permitting and building codes and would roll back county requirements beyond state law.

safety.basis: Co-sponsored a charter mandate for deputy staffing and calls for "unapologetically pro law enforcement" officials.

experience.basis: Cites county-office and charter-commission experience to "hit the ground running" while campaigning on "Leading for a Change"; has not held a governing seat.
